To render greater flexibility in generation, DIGEST repurposes a pretrained decoder block from a lightweight LLM into a symbolic policy for Genetic Programming (GP) population seeding, thereby leveraging the broader modeling capacity of the LLM. To more thoroughly utilize search discoveries, high-quality expressions discovered by GP are fed back to update the LLM-derived policy online, thereby enabling the LLM to progressively internalize past search discoveries and translate them into improved subsequent population generation. Experiments show that on two ground-truth benchmarks, DIGEST outperforms the strongest competitor by up to 2.59% in recovery. Among LLM-based baselines, it improves recovery by at least 54.91% while using at most 17.4% of the strongest competitor's mean search time. On 122 BlackBox datasets, DIGEST achieves the highest accuracy while maintaining a moderate model complexity.
papers.tldr: TL;DR: DIGESTは、データから数学的表現を発見するシンボリック回帰のために、軽量LLMの事前学習済みデコーダーブロックを利用して生成の柔軟性を高め、遺伝的プログラミングによって発見された高品質な表現をLLMポリシーにフィードバックすることで、表現の回復精度を向上させる手法です。実験では、DIGESTが競合他社を最大2.59%上回り、LLMベースの手法に対しては回復率を54.91%以上

papers.title: Semantic Concept Steering Breaks the Explanation Drift Loop in Continual Learning
papers.summary: Catastrophic forgetting in continual learning (CL) manifests not only as accuracy degradation but also as \emph{explanation drift}: models maintain predictive accuracy while silently shifting attention from diagnostic features to spurious correlations. This work identifies and resolves a previously overlooked structural flaw in explanation-aware CL: pixel-level saliency regularization derives supervision targets from the model's own frozen saliency maps, creating a \emph{self-referential drift loop} that actively reinforces spurious attention across tasks. We introduce \textbf{C$^3$L} (Concept-Consistent Continual Learning), which breaks this loop by anchoring regularization to class-consistent semantic concepts (e.g., ``curved beak'', ``striped pattern'') discovered offline, independent of model state, providing (i) target independence from model drift, and (ii) cross-instance semantic consistency across every instance of a class. We identify that our concept-based objective, combined with approximate LRP relevance conservation, induces a \emph{crowding-out effect}: since concept and background regions compete for the relevance of the same prediction, enforcing high relevance within concept regions implicitly suppresses spurious background correlations without explicit penalization. \method does not require human-annotated concept sets, as it employs a fully automated concept discovery and spatial grounding. Extensive evaluation across five benchmarks and over 20 baselines demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in accuracy, forgetting, explanation quality, spurious correlation mitigation, and out-of-distribution robustness.
papers.tldr: C$^3$L（Concept-Consistent Continual Learning）は、連続学習における説明の漂流ループを解消し、モデルがスパuriousな相関に注意を向けるのを防ぐために、クラス一貫性のあるセマンティックコンセプトに基づく正則化を導入し、精度や説明の質を向上させる手法です。

papers.title: FlashScript: Compiling Recurring Agent Workflows into Reusable Neuro-Symbolic Programs
papers.summary: Many agent tasks recur with new data or small changes, yet agents regenerate their reasoning and actions on each run, producing different results. Distilling a prior run into a skill helps the agent avoid earlier mistakes, but it still re-runs the full process each time, so runs can vary and incur that cost. We compile a successful agent run into a reusable neuro-symbolic program (NSP) with a set of guidelines we call FlashScript. Actions and data transformations become code, instance-specific values become parameters, and decisions that need model judgment become LLM calls. We identify three layers where these calls belong and three techniques that replace most of them with code. The compilation does not remove nondeterminism; it localizes it, so the deterministic program and its neural calls can be reviewed and tested separately. Across 120 WorkBench analytics tasks with Claude Haiku 4.5, the NSPs were correct and made identical tool calls on every run, using about 70 times fewer input tokens and a third of the runtime of a skill-guided agent whose runs were inconsistent. In a composite version of the tasks, the skill-guided agent's accuracy fell to 23%, and its output inconsistency increased, while the NSPs remained correct and identical across all runs. The NSPs successfully generalized to all 108 unseen instances of the same templates. Our findings suggest that NSPs from agent trajectories can be considered cumulative software assets for end-users to test, maintain, and reuse in their recurring workflows.
papers.tldr: FlashScriptは、エージェントの成功した実行を再利用可能な神経シンボリックプログラム（NSP）にコンパイルする手法で、これによりエージェントは以前の誤りを避けつつ、各実行での結果の一貫性を保ちながら、入力トークンを約70倍削減し、実行時間を3分の1に短縮できることを示しました。NSPは、異なるインスタンスでも正確に機能し、エンドユーザーが再利用可能なソフトウェア資産として活用できることが確認されました。
